newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish conscientious objector faces jail term.
newsitem.headline: Turkish conscientious objector faces jail term.

text.p: A military prosecutor on Tuesday demanded a two-year jail sentence for a 26-year-old Turkish peace protestor who refuses to do national service.

Prosecutor Faruk Ozeroglu said Osman Murat Ulke had broken article 155 of the Turkish penal code which bans "all propaganda aiming to break national strength and alienate the public from the military."

Ulke, head of the banned War Resisters' Association in the western city of Izmir, last year burned his military draft documents publicly and told a news conference he would refuse to take part in any form of military service.

"I am not the one alienating people from the military, but you, as the military, who force thousands of people into a meaningless war," Ulke told the court. He was referring to Turkey's 12-year-old fight with separatist Kurdish rebels.
Turkish laws do not allow any room for conscientious objection to military service, legally compulsory for up to 18 months for every Turkish male from 20 years of age.
Several other members of the association, and members of peaceful religious movements have been jailed in the past for refusing to do national service.
Ulke, a leather producer, denied encouraging others to refuse conscription.
In jail since October 8, Ulke was released by the court on the condition that he stay at the military base where he was originally assigned. His trial will continue on December 24.
